3 stars

Harbourline built out my mobile grooming van in August, and I have been trying to figure out how to review them ever since. The short version is that the build is great, the leak was a mess, and the way it was handled at first made it worse. They did come around in the end.

The good stuff first, because there's a lot of it. The stainless tub with the ramp and tether rail is easily the best thing about my van. Dogs walk right up the ramp like they're boarding a cruise ship, and my back has thanked me every day since. The layout, the cabinetry and the drain are all well thought out, and the van does what I need it to do all day, every day. If you want a grooming fitout, the craftsmanship is real.

Now the leak. On October 27th I was in Bedford with a 110 lb Bernese named Moose in the tub, mid-groom, when a fitting on the hot water line just let go. Water everywhere. Water down into the cabinet. Water doing things I did not know water could do. I was screaming, a little. Moose was not. Moose sat in that tub like a king watching his kingdom flood, calm as anything, possibly enjoying the spa package. I towelled him off, sent him home half done, and cancelled the rest of my day.

I emailed Glenn right away. His reply was that these lines don't just let go, that it was probably user error, and that it wouldn't be covered under warranty. He also said the earliest he could see the van was Tuesday, November 3rd, with a $180 diagnostic fee to look at it. For the record, I had not run the heater dry and nobody hangs things off a pipe that lives behind a cabinet door. A week out was a long wait for me, since I ended up cancelling 6 bookings on top of that lost day.

That "user error" line is what actually got me. Stuff breaks, and I know that. I run a business with a van, a dryer and a lot of water, and I don't expect anything to be perfect. But being told it was probably my fault before anyone had looked at it stung, especially when I was the one eating the lost bookings and paying to find out.

To Glenn's credit, here's how it ended. Once the van was in, he found that the compression fitting on the outlet was a cheaper one his supplier had swapped in. He said so plainly, said it was on them, and replaced all of the fittings on the hot side. He also took the $180 off. I appreciate that, because plenty of shops would have dug in. The van came back on November 6th, so it was off the road from October 27th to November 6th, and it has been fine since.

So where does that leave me? The build work gets a very solid grade. The first response to the leak gets a much lower one, and the repair and the ownership at the end bring it back up. That averages out to three stars for me. I'd happily have given more if the "user error" assumption hadn't come before the diagnosis.

A tip for other groomers and anyone else getting a trade or mobile business van built:

Get the warranty details in writing, and read them closely. Mine covers workmanship for 12 months but excludes misuse and user error, which is a very flexible phrase when something goes wrong on day 70. Ask up front what counts as user error, who covers diagnostic fees if the fault turns out to be the shop's or their supplier's, and ask what parts they're using. It's a better conversation to have at the start than in the middle of a flood.

Would I go back to Harbourline? For a build, probably yes, with the warranty questions asked first. And Moose has given the whole thing a full five stars.
